messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 99p latency on streaming endpoints (us-west-2). Errors +4% over baseline, throughput contended. Auto-detection triggered.
jordan: acknowledged, paging oncall. I'll start a quick check of traces.
hani: oncall here — digging in. any immediate customer reports?
incident-bot: Top traces show long-running sessions with token churn causing kernel stalls; mux queue depth increasing, GPU utilization ~85% with intermittent stalls.
maya: seeing repeated frame retransmits on mux layer, looks like streaming backpressure. Suggest temporary degradation of streaming output to reduce tail.
alex: can we switch to safemode: disable streaming frames and return final-chunk responses instead? That should reduce continuous emitter load.
jordan: if we flip that, we must also tighten rate limits to prevent thundering herd when clients poll for final data. Proposal: disable streaming for redwood-7b-v1 in us-west-2, QPS cap per-key 50->10, and fall back to final-response mode.
hani: agree. I'll run the toggle in ~5m and monitor SLOs. Support - please prep customer comms.
support-lead: will notify tier1 and surface any active enterprise customers. Which customers might see UX regression?
maya: mostly PLG chats and free-tier sessions. No Dedicated tenants in this AZ on the affected model.
alex: command I'll run: `/toggle-feature streaming-responses --scope=region:us-west-2 --model=redwood-7b-v1 --value=false`
jordan: go for it. I'll open a live dashboard and share.
deploy-bot: Executing toggle... ETA ~30s.
jordan: Dashboard link: https://dash.internal/realtime?m=redwood-7b-v1&region=us-west-2 - watching GPU stalls and mux queues.
deploy-bot: Toggle complete. streaming-responses=false for redwood-7b-v1 in us-west-2.
hani: monitoring metrics now — 99p latency dropped 2.1s -> 0.8s within 2 minutes.
maya: :thumbsup: nice. Now applying QPS cap: `/set-rate-limit --scope=region:us-west-2 --qps=10`
ops-runner: Rate caps applied. Connections evened out, error rate trending down.
support-lead: posted status update: "We are temporarily disabling streaming responses in us-west-2 to stabilize latency. Final-response mode active; teams are monitoring."
alex: also enabling prefix KV caching for common prompts to shave repeat token work.
jordan: collecting any session IDs with 500s for post-incident followup. Support, escalate any high-severity customer tickets.
support-lead: will watch the queue and notify if enterprise customers report issues.
maya: rollback criteria: 99p < 1s and error rate < 0.5% for a sustained 10m window, then canary re-enable streaming at 5%.
hani: agreed. handoff: I'm passing to night-oncall in 40m — will DM the playbook and steps.
night-oncall: taking handoff. Confirmed runbook and will monitor until midnight.
jordan: creating PD incident and timeline notes.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC1234567 - "Streaming safemode toggle to stabilize us-west-2"
maya: postmortem owner suggestion: eng-runtime + eng-sre.
jordan: I'll own the postmortem and gather logs/timeline.
support-lead: if anything changes, set channel to #priority-incident and ping SRE pager.
night-oncall: noted — monitoring now. :eyes:
